assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting artificial atom routine and supplied the dispersive readout, two-qubit coupling and bus architecture that nearly every superconducting processor uses. It is original, clearly defined and has had lasting, field-defining impact. It also follows naturally from the macroscopic quantum circuit physics recognised in 2025.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the 2004 theory proposal with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf. Wallraff and Schoelkopf carried out the 2004 Nature strong-coupling experiments in the Yale group. The three credited names form a clean, defensible trio. Credit for the other 2004 co-authors (Girvin, Huang, Majer and others) and for the Yale experimental group is a recognised allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: reproduced and extended in dozens of laboratories over two decades, and used in multi-qubit gates, error-correction demonstrations and microwave quantum optics. The interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, with only a mild risk that it looks too close to the 2025 prize.
uncertainties: I work in this area and direct a related centre, so my familiarity with it may bias my reading of its importance.
The overlap with the 2025 circuit-based prize may count against it with colleagues, and I cannot verify how that is weighed.
Girvin's and Devoret's roles in the founding theory and experiment might call for a different configuration, which I cannot resolve from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened the entire field of moire quantum matter. It is a very original, tunable platform for strongly correlated physics with enormous follow-on activity.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the decisive 2011 theory. Jarillo-Herrero led the 2018 experiments, with Cao as lead author and the Fatemi/Cao group at MIT. The supplied credit supports a theory-plus-experiment trio. Contributions by Dean and Kim on related moire systems, and the junior experimental authors, may complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups within a few years and still expanding. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, which is a maturity caution. The platform and the observation of correlated states are secure.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene remains contested.
Other moire discoveries (for example fractional Chern insulators) are separate and may need independent recognition.
I am not an expert in 2D materials, so my judgement of priority here is less informed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, from Katori's magic-wavelength proposal to Ye's strontium clocks reaching 1e-18 fractional uncertainty, are a transformative advance in precision measurement. They open tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The concept is clear and the impact lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2001-2003. Ye's group demonstrated the highest performance and the many-body and spin-polarised clock work. A two-person prize is plausible. Contributions of Hall (already honoured in 2005) and others in the comb and clock lineage are separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced by several national laboratories. Timing is good as the redefinition of the second approaches, though that redefinition has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: The lineage with the 2005 and 2012 prizes for frequency combs and trapped-ion control could be read as a continuation rather than a new discovery.
Whether Ye alone or additional lattice-clock pioneers (for example Lemonde, Lisdat) merit credit cannot be settled from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 key distribution founded quantum cryptography, with security rooted in the no-cloning and measurement principles of quantum mechanics. It is conceptually original, widely taught and underpins a developing technology. The physics content is clear, though the work is more information-theoretic than a dynamical discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the unambiguous originators of BB84 in 1984. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is an independent and important contribution, so a prize might sensibly include him. I propose the two originators and note that the supplied credit leaves this choice open.
assessment.maturity: Protocols have been demonstrated in fibre and satellite links, and loophole-free Bell tests relate to device-independent security. Practical deployment is still limited, and hacking of implementations is an ongoing concern, but the foundational idea is mature and secure.
uncertainties: Whether Ekert should displace or join Bennett and Brassard is a genuine attribution question.
Physics versus computer-science character of the work may affect its fit with the physics prize.
Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not among the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, together with the HgTe experiment, created a major branch of condensed matter physics and a conceptual framework for topological band structure. The importance and originality are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive 2005 theory. Molenkamp's group made the 2007 HgTe observation, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not among the supplied names. Hasan's ARPES work on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 is also central to 3D topological insulators, so a three-name limit forces a hard allocation. I choose the theory and the first experimental confirmation.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with many materials and independent confirmations. The field has already been partly recognised through the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions, so the novelty relative to that prize must be argued.
uncertainties: Credit for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and for Hasan is unresolved within three slots.
Overlap with the 2016 topological matter prize may be seen as weakening novelty.
Applied consequences such as dissipationless edge transport remain limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade in tweezer arrays enabled programmable many-body quantum simulators and high-fidelity neutral-atom gates, with demonstrations of large arrays, quantum phases and early error-correction logic. The impact on quantum simulation and computing is large and growing quickly.
assessment.attribution: Saffman contributed the blockade-gate proposals and demonstrations, Browaeys the early tweezer-array experiments, and Lukin the large programmable arrays and quantum-phase work. Jaksch, Zoller and Weiss are also important in the foundations and are not among the supplied names, so attribution is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly advancing and independently reproduced, but still maturing; claims of fault-tolerant scaling are recent and the interpretation of long-term significance is not settled. I consider recognition somewhat early.
uncertainties: Strong dependence on a still-evolving technology; recognition may be premature.
Credit for the theory of the Rydberg blockade (Jaksch, Lukin and colleagues) versus the experiments is difficult to split.
Overlap with ion-trap and lattice-based quantum simulation recognised in other prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the later theory of quantum simulation with cold atoms provided the concrete architecture that experiments then realised. The ideas are original and have been influential across atomic and quantum-information physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are a natural pair, and the supplied credit consists of just those two. Experimental realisation by Wineland (2012 prize) and Blatt is related but separate. The pair's later work spans many sub-themes, so a single-discovery framing is not tidy.
assessment.maturity: The ion-trap gate proposal has been confirmed and extended extensively, and the work is mature. Parts of the quantum-simulation programme are still developing.
uncertainties: The theory may be read as already partly encompassed by the 2012 prize for ion control.
Which single discovery to cite is ambiguous, since their contributions span multiple areas.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics showed radiation-pressure cooling of mechanical oscillators to the quantum ground state, quantum-limited readout and quantum states of macroscopic mechanics. It connects closely to the superconducting circuit and microwave-resonator toolbox and is physically clear.
assessment.attribution: Kippenberg demonstrated early radiation-pressure cooling and strong coupling, Aspelmeyer pioneered cooling and the fundamentals, and Painter contributed nanoscale optomechanical crystals and ground-state results. Cleland, Lehnert and Teufel also achieved ground-state cooling in the microwave domain and are not among the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally well confirmed in many platforms, with applications in sensing and transduction. Broader impact beyond the field is still developing, so recognition is a bit early.
uncertainties: Ground-state cooling credit is shared among several groups beyond the supplied names.
The scientific reach beyond optomechanics itself is less proven than that of the higher-ranked candidates.
